name: Legendary MoneyMon zero-signer claim bypass
summary: LegendaryMoneyMonNft.verify compares raw ecrecover output with admin without rejecting the zero address. After the owner sets admin to zero, an invalid 65-byte signature recovers zero and authorizes cliamRewred to transfer an arbitrary ERC20 balance to the caller.

loss.notes: The complete MON reserve was stolen and sold in the same transaction for 85519.468029991188020606 BSC USDT, valued at USD parity. The effective MON price uses actual disposal rather than a reserve quote. No attacker principal entered the MON reserve. Gas and later recovery do not reduce gross loss. The other successful zero-signer claim withdrew one test token from 11 previously supplied by that caller and adds no victim loss.

ageReset.description: changeadmin(address(0)) changes the signer from a nonzero address to zero, making ecrecover failure satisfy the deployed authorization check.

sources.note: Reviewed anchor, root cause, loss, artifact identity and complete age history. Etherscan V2 getsourcecode returns verified LegendaryMoneyMonNft, compiler v0.8.14. cliamRewred (0x33444682) checks unused signature bytes, verify, nonzero payment address and positive amount, then transfers the caller-selected ERC20 amount to msg.sender. It does not require the caller to own an NFT. verify hashes the claim and compares recoverSigner directly with admin. splitSignature requires 65 bytes but recoverSigner returns ecrecover without rejecting zero. Source-1 callTracer reaches the victim directly from EIP-7702 account 0xe1582248c593df4b367e131922438fec9d76e787, calls precompile 0x01 with v=27 and r=s=0, then transfers its entire MON reserve to that account. The delegated attacker implementation is attack machinery, not the aged artifact. Source-3 receipt anchors direct CREATE at 82850902:76 by the owner. Code is empty at 82850901 and the 19739-byte runtime hashes identically at creation, 100929540, 100937038 and source-1 prestateTracer. Verified source has no upgrade, delegation or destruction path. The only admin write after initialization is changeadmin, protected by onlyOwner. Complete Etherscan victim txlist has 782 transactions through the coverage scan, with two changeadmin calls: source-4 sets zero and source-5 restores a nonzero signer. The owner txlist from creation through the exploit has 18 transactions. Their callTracers contain only source-4 calling this victim setter, ruling out an internal reset through another owner transaction. Source-4 prestateTracer diff identifies slot 0x0d changing from 0x000000000000000000000000a8cf7acc731b17e06a0b4c7cc79ce02cd51cfa59 to zero. admin() (0xf851a440) independently returns the former value at 100929540 and zero at 100929541 and 100937038. Reproduce verify(address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,string,bytes) with payment=MON, user=the attacker, nftid=1, amount=24306531592912737187217, time=1779977792, exname="1", signature=64 zero bytes followed by 0x1b. The identical message returns false at 100929540 and true at 100929541. This proves that the zero-signer state creates the bypass, rather than merely increasing exposure, so source-4 is the latest causal age reset, 3388 seconds before source-1. Source-5 at 100969407:37 sets admin to 0x23f6c590fd18d8ea827859168546be4cbc5f4a2e, which admin() still returns at coverage block 125541856. Scan the victim eventname(string,address,uint256,bool,uint256,uint256,uint256) topic 0x8240417e1fd64b2e3dc8ce76497682b290ea79c02323f85a77d384664f272361 from deployment through 125541856 in 1000000-block intervals. It returns 94 events. The only two with first string calimrewred are source-1 and source-7. Every successful cliamRewred emits this event, so source-1 is the first successful exercise and the scan covers recurrences. Source-7 at 100942034:66 uses another invalid signature to withdraw 1e18 units of token 0x0e317205eb8db594fdfb2d560665f376c4f7a67f. That caller, 0x6863dc1f9ee49f58d460490f7053f8ab79865bb0, supplied 11e18 units in source-8 at 100941927:38. The token Transfer-to-victim history contains only that input, so this later exercise returns caller-supplied principal and adds no victim loss. In source-1, MON balanceOf(victim) returns 24306531592912737187217 and receipt log 48 transfers exactly that amount to the attacker. Historical symbol/name/decimals are MON/Moneymon/18. The attacker initially holds no MON, sells the entire stolen quantity through PancakeSwap v3 pool 0x20bdcd1387fee20e42c3b4d328c9d3ad2dea9e1d, and logs 51/52 show 85519468029991188020606 USDT received and all stolen MON paid to that pool. BSC USDT has 18 decimals. At USD parity, divide those proceeds by the stolen MON quantity for the effective unit value. No financing, gas, builder or recovery adjustment is applied. Future updates should extend the claim-event scan and check renewed zero-signer configuration before merging later claims.
